mainTopic: The burial town of יהושע and כלב's portion, then a new משנה comparing sons and daughters in inheritance, and how big the בכור's double portion is.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion of people who received land outside the lottery. The גמרא notes that יהושע's burial town is called 'סרח' in one פסוק and 'חרס' in another, and explains that the two names describe its fruit at different stages. It then shows that כלב received חברון. Since חברון was an עיר מקלט, אביי explains that כלב got only the surrounding fields. Next comes a new משנה: son and daughter are alike in inheritance, but a בכור's double portion and the daughters' support come only from the father's estate. The גמרא asks what 'alike' means. It rejects three readings, from רב נחמן בר יצחק, רב פפא and רב אשי, because each either repeats another משנה or fails to explain the word 'אלא'. Finally, מר בר רב אשי explains that sons and daughters inherit from both parents, and the בכור's double portion comes only from the father's estate. A ברייתא then begins to discuss whether the double portion is double one heir's share or two-thirds of the whole estate.

steps.title: Two different names for יהושע's burial town
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one פסוק calls יהושע's town 'סרח' and another calls it 'חרס'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'סרח', and it is written 'חרס'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that two פסוקים give two different names for the same town where יהושע was buried, and it wants to know why. This sets up the next step, where an answer is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of סרח and חרס are the same letters in reverse order. The question is not about which name is right. The גמרא assumes both are right and asks what each name teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (in a פסוק)
Part of the town name תמנת סרח
Clay or earthenware; part of the town name תמנת חרס

phrases.english: It is written: 'Serah',
phrases.notes: יהושע 24:30, where יהושע is buried in תמנת סרח.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Heres'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of יהושע's special portion by pointing out a contradiction between two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two different names for יהושע's town in two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same place appears with two different names, so something needs to explain the difference.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the fruits changed from hard to overripe
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that both names describe the town's fruits at different times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: At first its fruits were like clay, and in the end its fruits were spoiling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that both names are true. Each name describes the town's fruit at a different stage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חרס (clay) describes fruit that is dry and hard. סרח sounds like מסריחין, meaning spoiling from being so juicy and ripe. So חרס describes the early, poor fruit and סרח describes the later, very ripe fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: At first
Its fruits
Spoiling, rotting (word play on סרח)
In the end

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
at first its fruits were like clay,
phrases.notes: He means dry and hard, like a piece of pottery.

phrases.english: and in the end its fruits were spoiling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: בַּתְּחִלָּה פֵּירוֹתֶיהָ כְּחֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both פסוקים are correct; each name describes a different time period.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two names seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: חרס describes the early dry fruit and סרח describes the later juicy, overripe fruit.

steps.title: Another version: the fruits changed from spoiling to long-lasting
steps.stepSummary: Others reverse the order: at first the fruit spoiled quickly, and later it lasted like clay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: At first they were spoiling, and in the end they were like clay.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version of the answer is brought, with the order flipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here חרס is read as a good thing: the fruit lasted a long time without rotting, the way clay does not rot. סרח becomes the earlier, worse stage, when the fruit spoiled too quickly. Both versions agree that the two names describe two stages of the fruit.
steps.confusionAlert: In this version חרס is the good stage (lasting fruit). In רבי אלעזר's version it was the bad stage (hard fruit). Don't mix up which stage each version praises.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
at first they were spoiling,
and in the end they were like clay.
phrases.notes: Now 'like clay' is a compliment: the fruit kept for a long time without going bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of רבי אלעזר's answer with the order reversed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same idea of two time periods, but the order of the stages is reversed.
steps.terutzMaskana: First the fruit spoiled quickly (סרח); later it lasted like clay (חרס).

steps.title: כלב also received a special portion: חברון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק showing that כלב was given חברון, as משה had promised.
steps.simpleTranslation: כלב: as it is written, 'And they gave חברון to כלב, as משה had said, and he drove out from there the three sons of the giant.'
steps.whatsHappening: Moving on from יהושע, the גמרא shows that כלב also got his own special portion, and quotes the פסוק that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'As משה had said' shows that this land was promised to כלב personally and was not won in the lottery. This sets up the question in the next step about how חברון could be given to him.

keyTerms.meaning: כלב בן יפונה, one of the two loyal spies
The city of חברון
The sons of the giant (ענק)

phrases.english: Caleb, as it is written:
'And they gave Hebron to Caleb
as Moses had spoken,
and he drove out from there
the three sons of the giant.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יהושע's portion to כלב's portion, the next item in the earlier list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלב received חברון as a special gift, as משה promised, not through the lottery.

steps.title: But חברון was a city of refuge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: חברון was an עיר מקלט, so how could it be given to כלב?
steps.simpleTranslation: חברון was a city of refuge!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that חברון was an עיר מקלט, so it could not simply have been given to כלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cities of refuge were set aside as cities of the לוים (here, the כהנים). If חברון was one of them, it seems it could not belong to כלב.

keyTerms.meaning: City of refuge for someone who killed by accident
Was (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Hebron was a city of refuge!
phrases.notes: In יהושע 21:13, חברון is given to the כהנים as a city of refuge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of step 4 that כלב received חברון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוק saying חברון was given to כלב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A city of refuge belonged to the כהנים, so it could not be כלב's private portion.

steps.title: אביי: כלב got only the outskirts
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that כלב received only the fields and villages around חברון, and proves it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Its outskirts, as it is written, 'And the fields of the city and its villages they gave to כלב בן יפונה as his possession.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the problem: the city itself went to the כהנים as an עיר מקלט, while כלב got the land around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'gave חברון to כלב' is narrowed to mean the surrounding area (פרוורהא). The פסוק in יהושע says this outright, so there is no contradiction. The city stays an עיר מקלט, and כלב's portion is the outskirts.

keyTerms.meaning: Its outskirts, the area around the city
The fields of the city
Its villages (here, the open settlements around the city)
His possession, his land holding

steps.whatToRemember: Both יהושע (תמנת סרח) and כלב (the outskirts of חברון) received special portions. כלב did not get the city itself, which remained an עיר מקלט.

phrases.english: Abaye said: its outskirts,
as it is written: 'But the fields of the city
and its villages they gave
to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows what was given: the outskirts only, proven from a פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כלב received the whole city of חברון, which clashes with its status as an עיר מקלט.
steps.terutzMaskana: The city was an עיר מקלט for the כהנים; כלב received the fields and villages around it.

steps.title: New משנה: son and daughter in inheritance, and two differences
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says son and daughter are alike in נחלה, but the firstborn son gets a double portion only from the father, and daughters are supported only from the father's estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The son and the daughter are the same regarding inheritance, except that the son takes a double portion of the father's property but not of the mother's property. And the daughters are supported from the father's property but not from the mother's property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says sons and daughters are alike in inheritance, then gives two differences between the father's estate and the mother's estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first difference is that a בכור gets פי שנים only from his father, not his mother. The second is that daughters receive מזונות from the father's estate (part of their mother's כתובה) but not from the mother's estate. The opening line 'alike in inheritance' is unclear, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Inheritance
A double portion (of the firstborn)
The father's property
Are supported, fed (receive מזונות)

steps.confusionAlert: 'The son' in the double-portion line means the firstborn son (בכור), not every son.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Both the son and the daughter are alike in inheritance;
except that the son takes a double portion
phrases.notes: The משנה means the firstborn son here.

phrases.english: of the father's property,
but he does not take a double portion
of the mother's property.
And the daughters are supported from the father's property,
but they are not supported from the mother's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the discussion of the land portions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Son and daughter are alike in inheritance; a בכור takes פי שנים only from the father; daughters get מזונות only from the father's estate.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two rules (the firstborn's double portion and daughters' support) are basic inheritance laws that the rest of the sugya will examine.

steps.title: What does 'son and daughter are alike' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means when it says son and daughter are alike in inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'both the son and the daughter are alike in inheritance'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its study of the משנה by asking what its first line means. This sets up the challenge that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line can't simply mean that sons and daughters share equally, as the next step will show. So the גמרא needs to work out exactly how they are 'alike'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What (does it mean)?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is meant by 'both the son and the daughter are alike in inheritance'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's first clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way are a son and a daughter equal regarding inheritance?

steps.title: They can't inherit together, because a son comes first
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה means they inherit together, that contradicts the earlier משנה that a son and all his descendants come before a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they inherit together, didn't we learn: A son comes before a daughter, and all the descendants of a son come before a daughter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simplest reading, that sons and daughters inherit side by side, and rejects it using an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה (115a) taught that a son pushes away a daughter, and so does anyone descended from the son. So a daughter does not inherit together with a son, and the משנה's words must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposing a reading in order to reject it)
Together, alike with each other
But we learned (in a משנה)
His descendants (literally, those who come from his thigh)

phrases.english: If we say that they inherit together,
but didn't we learn: a son precedes a daughter,
all the descendants of a son
precede a daughter!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּיָרְתִי כִּי הֲדָדֵי, הָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a first answer to the question of step 8 and immediately challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that sons and daughters inherit together equally.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier משנה rules that a son and all his descendants come before a daughter, so they cannot inherit side by side.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: Both inherit 'due' property like owned property
steps.stepSummary: After a memory sign, רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the משנה means son and daughter both inherit property that was due to the father, the same way they inherit property he already held.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: נפש״ם.) רב נחמן בר יצחק said: This is what the משנה means. Both a son and a daughter take property that was due to come to the father, just like property he already owned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to read the משנה so it no longer clashes with the rule that a son comes before a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 showed the משנה can't mean son and daughter inherit together. רב נחמן בר יצחק says 'alike' means something else: whichever one inherits takes both kinds of property, ראוי and מוחזק.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign that helps you remember the order of the Sages in the discussion
'This is what it is saying': introduces a new reading of a text
Property that was due to come to someone but that he had not yet received
Property someone already owned and held

phrases.english: (Memory sign: Nafsham.)
phrases.notes: The letters stand for the Sages coming up in this discussion: נחמן, פפא, אשי, מר.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
This is what it is saying:
Both the son and the daughter
take property that was due, just as they take property that was held.
phrases.notes: 'Due' means property the father was about to get but never received, like an inheritance that hadn't reached him yet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 9 by giving the משנה a new meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Alike' seemed to mean son and daughter inherit side by side
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Alike' means each inherits ראוי the same as מוחזק

steps.title: This was already taught in the case of בנות צלפחד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that we already know ראוי is inherited like מוחזק from the משנה about בנות צלפחד, so our משנה would be repeating it for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this: the daughters of צלפחד took three portions in the inheritance. They took their father's portion as one of those who left Egypt, and his portion with his brothers in חפר's property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading by pointing out it would make the משנה say something already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צלפחד died before his father חפר, so his share in חפר's estate was only ראוי. Even so, his daughters inherited it. That earlier משנה already proves ראוי is inherited, so why would our משנה need to teach it again?

keyTerms.meaning: 'We already learned this too': a challenge that a teaching is unnecessary
The daughters of צלפחד, who inherited their father's land
Those who left Egypt, who each got a share of ארץ ישראל
צלפחד's father

phrases.english: This too we have already learned:
Zelophehad's daughters took
three portions in the inheritance:
their father's portion
since he was among those who left Egypt,
and his portion together with his brothers
in the property of Hepher!
phrases.notes: צלפחד died before חפר, so this share was only 'due' to him. The third portion, his extra share as a firstborn, isn't quoted here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation from step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading makes our משנה repeat a rule already taught about בנות צלפחד

steps.title: His reading doesn't fit the word 'but'
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: according to רב נחמן בר יצחק, what contrast is the word 'אלא' in the משנה making?
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, what is the meaning of 'but'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second objection, based on how the משנה is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says son and daughter are alike, 'but' the firstborn takes double from the father and not from the mother. That 'אלא' contrasts the father's property with the mother's, so the first clause should be about both parents. A first clause about ראוי and מוחזק says nothing about the mother, so the 'but' has nothing to contrast with.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And furthermore': introduces a second challenge
'But': a word that marks a contrast with what came before

phrases.english: And furthermore,
what is meant by "but"?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's 'but the firstborn takes double from the father's property and not the mother's'. A 'but' needs a clear contrast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent attack on the explanation in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'אלא' needs a contrast with the first clause, and his reading gives none

steps.title: רב פפא: Son and daughter both receive the firstborn's share
steps.stepSummary: Since רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading failed, רב פפא explains that the son or daughter of a firstborn receives the firstborn's extra portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: This is what the משנה means. Both a son and a daughter take the portion of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the previous explanation and gives a new one from רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'alike' is about בכורה: whichever child inherits from a firstborn, even a daughter, gets his double share. This no longer says son and daughter inherit side by side. But the next two steps attack it on the same two grounds used against רב נחמן בר יצחק: it repeats an earlier משנה, and it doesn't fit 'אלא'.

keyTerms.meaning: The firstborn's right to an extra (double) portion
A double portion, the firstborn's share

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reading (ראוי like מוחזק) was rejected twice: it repeats an earlier משנה, and it doesn't fit 'אלא'. רב פפא reads the משנה as being about passing on the firstborn's share.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
This is what it is saying:
Both the son and the daughter
take a portion of the firstborn's share.
phrases.notes: He means the children of a firstborn, even a daughter, receive that firstborn's extra share.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that steps 11 and 12 rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Alike' meant inheriting ראוי the same as מוחזק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Alike' means son or daughter both receive a firstborn's extra share (a reading the גמרא goes on to reject in steps 14-15)

steps.title: רב פפא's reading repeats an earlier משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a בכור taking a double portion is already taught in the משנה about בנות צלפחד.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this too: 'and because he was a בכור, who takes two portions!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's explanation from Step 13. It says the משנה would be teaching something we already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה about בנות צלפחד says they took an extra share because their father was a בכור. That already shows a בכור's children get his double portion. So reading our משנה that way makes it a pointless repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned this too (in another משנה)
Firstborn son
Two portions, the firstborn's double share

phrases.english: This too we have already learned:
phrases.notes: He means the משנה about the daughters of צלפחד, which the גמרא used back in Step 11.

phrases.english: "and since he was a firstborn, he takes two portions!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from Step 13, the same way Step 11 challenged רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should not repeat a law that another משנה already teaches.

steps.title: רב פפא's reading cannot explain the word 'but'
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: under רב פפא's reading, the contrast made by 'אלא' in the משנה makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, what is the 'but'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem to רב פפא's reading. It is the same question that was asked of רב נחמן בר יצחק in Step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה goes on to say 'but a בכור takes double from the father, not from the mother.' That 'but' only makes sense if the first part of the משנה was about inheriting from both parents. רב פפא's reading has nothing to do with the mother, so the contrast has nothing to contrast with.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (a second objection)
But / except; here the contrasting word in the משנה

phrases.english: And furthermore, what is the "but"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate attack on רב פפא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'אלא' needs a real contrast with the first part of the משנה, and this reading does not provide one.

steps.title: רב אשי: a father may give everything to one child
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the משנה lets a father leave all his property to one son among sons, or to one daughter among daughters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: This is what the משנה means. Whether it is one son among the sons or one daughter among the daughters, if the father said 'He shall inherit all my property,' his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב פפא's reading failed, רב אשי offers a new explanation of the משנה. He says it is about a father choosing one heir to get everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'a son and a daughter are equal' means that each can be named as sole heir. A father can name any one son, and when there are no sons he can name any one daughter. This works because each of them is someone who would inherit from him anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a new reading of the text)
He shall inherit all my property
His words stand (they take effect)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said, this is what it is saying:
Whether a son among the sons
or a daughter among the daughters,
if he said: "He shall inherit all my property"
– his words stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב פפא's rejected reading with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was about inheriting a בכור's portion (רב פפא).
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that a father may name one son, or one daughter when there are no sons, as sole heir.

steps.title: This is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's view, taught later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that רב אשי's rule is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's opinion, which a later משנה already teaches in his name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom? Like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא?! But the משנה teaches that later: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says, if he said it about someone fit to inherit from him, his words stand. If he said it about someone not fit to inherit from him, his words do not stand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view רב אשי's reading follows. It answers that it can only be רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, and that is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's rule is that a father can give everything to someone who would inherit from him anyway. That is exactly רב אשי's reading. But the later משנה states this openly as his opinion, so why would our משנה teach it here too?

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? (whose opinion does this follow?)
Later on (in a later משנה)
Fit to inherit from him (a legal heir)

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka?!
But it is taught later on –
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר עַל מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ –
phrases.english: If he said it about someone fit to inherit from him –
his words stand;
about someone not fit to inherit from him –
his words do not stand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's new reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב אשי's reading, the משנה would repeat a rule that a later משנה gives openly in רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא's name.

steps.title: An unattributed ruling followed by a dispute does not set the halacha
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects a possible defense that the משנה repeats the rule anonymously to set the הלכה like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the משנה taught us an anonymous ruling following רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, this is a case of an anonymous ruling followed by a dispute. With an anonymous ruling followed by a dispute, the הלכה is not like the anonymous ruling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a way to save רב אשי's reading, then shoots it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The defense would be: our משנה states the rule with no name attached, a סתם, to show the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. But the later משנה presents his view in a dispute with other תנאים. The rule is that when a סתם comes first and a מחלוקת comes after it, we do not follow the סתם. So this repeat would accomplish nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (an imagined defense)
An anonymous ruling in a משנה, given with no name
An anonymous ruling followed later by a dispute on the same topic
The הלכה does not follow the anonymous ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Usually a סתם משנה does set the הלכה. Here the rule is reversed only because a מחלוקת on the same topic comes after it.
steps.whatToRemember: Both earlier readings and now רב אשי's reading run into the same problem: the משנה would be needlessly repeating a rule found elsewhere.

phrases.english: And if you would say:

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָתַם לַן כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא;
phrases.english: It taught us an anonymous ruling following Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka;
it is an anonymous ruling followed by a dispute,
and with an anonymous ruling followed by a dispute –
the halacha is not like the anonymous ruling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to the challenge in Step 17, which strengthens that challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that our משנה is a סתם meant to set the הלכה like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A סתם followed by a מחלוקת does not set the הלכה, so the repeat would serve no purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses a general rule for deciding הלכה from the order of משניות: סתם ואחר כך מחלוקת, אין הלכה כסתם.

steps.title: The word 'but' still makes no sense under רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second objection to רב אשי: under his reading, the 'אלא' contrast in the משנה has nothing to contrast with.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, what is the meaning of 'but'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא hits רב אשי's reading with the same problem it raised against רב פפא in Step 15: the word 'אלא' (but) doesn't fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב אשי, the first part of the משנה is about a father giving everything to one child. That first part says nothing about a mother's property. So the next line, 'but the בכור does not take double from the mother's property', has nothing to be contrasted with.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds another objection
What is the meaning of 'but'? It asks what the contrast is

phrases.english: And furthermore, what is 'but'?
phrases.notes: This is the same question the גמרא asked against רב פפא in Step 15, now aimed at רב אשי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to רב אשי, on top of Steps 17-18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading of the משנה (Step 16)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'אלא' clause contrasts father's property with mother's property, but under רב אשי the first clause never mentions a mother, so there is nothing to contrast.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: son and daughter both inherit from father and mother
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי reads the משנה as saying sons and daughters can inherit from both parents, and the difference is that the בכור's double portion applies to the father's property alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said: This is what the משנה means. A son and a daughter are the same, in that both inherit from the mother's property and from the father's property. The difference is that the son takes a double portion from the father's property but not from the mother's property.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב נחמן בר יצחק, רב פפא and רב אשי, the גמרא gives a new reading of the משנה from מר בר רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the first clause talks about both the mother's and the father's property. So the 'אלא' finally makes sense: both parents' property is inherited, but the double portion of a בכור applies only to the father's property. This answers the objection of Step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal; the same
The mother's property
The father's property
A double portion, which a בכור receives

steps.whatToRemember: The final reading of the משנה: sons and daughters inherit from both parents, but a בכור's double portion applies only to the father's estate.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rather, Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
This is what it is saying:
Both the son and the daughter are equal
with the mother's property and with the father's property,
but the son takes a double portion
phrases.notes: 'The son' here means the firstborn, the בכור.

phrases.english: of the father's property,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּנִכְסֵי הָאֵם.
phrases.english: and he does not take a double portion of the mother's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of רב אשי with a new reading
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the משנה (הכי קאמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's first clause was about giving all property to one child, or about the בכור's portion in general, which left 'אלא' with nothing to contrast.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause says both genders inherit from both parents; 'אלא' then limits the בכור's double portion to the father's property.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the double portion is double what one heir gets
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'פי שנים' in the פסוק means the בכור gets twice the share of one other heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'to give him a double portion' means double what one heir gets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a ברייתא explaining how big the בכור's double portion is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the double portion is measured against one brother's share. For example, with two sons, the estate is split into three parts: the בכור takes two and the other son takes one.

keyTerms.meaning: Double compared to one heir's share

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'To give him a double portion':
double compared to one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the size of the בכור's double portion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור receives twice the share of any single other heir.

steps.title: Double one share, or two-thirds of everything?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether 'double' really means double one heir's share, or maybe double compared to the whole rest of the estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means double compared to one heir, or perhaps it means double in all the property?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own reading by raising another possible meaning of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other option is that the בכור always takes two-thirds of the estate, double what all the other brothers together get. With only two sons both readings give the same result, but with more brothers they are very different.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you say... or perhaps it is only...; a ברייתא formula raising another possible reading
In all the property; the whole estate

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up: with two sons both readings give the בכור two-thirds. The argument only matters when there are three or more sons.

phrases.english: Do you say double compared to one,
or is it perhaps only double
in all the property?
phrases.notes: He means the בכור would take two-thirds of the whole estate, however many brothers there are.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר פִּי שְׁנַיִם כְּאֶחָד, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכׇל הַנְּכָסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading stated in Step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the double portion measured against one heir's share, or against the entire remaining estate?

steps.title: Opening a logical argument
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא announces that it will settle the question with a logical argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical:
steps.whatsHappening: This short line sets up the next move: the ברייתא is about to prove its answer with reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ודין הוא' tells us a proof from reasoning is coming, not from a פסוק. The actual argument appears in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is logical; introduces a proof from reasoning

phrases.english: And it is logical:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of Step 22
steps.raayaObject: That 'פי שנים' means double compared to one heir
steps.raayaSupportSource: A logical argument (דין), which continues in the next section
